title: Comparing Norwegian adjectives and adverbs
goal: Compare people, things, and actions with regular, long, and irregular adjective and adverb forms.

objectives.statement: Compare people, things, and actions with regular, long, and irregular adjective and adverb forms.

spans.value: Mina and Jonas are renting bicycles for a weekend trip. They must choose between two routes and several bikes.
Denne sykkelen er lettere enn den røde.

blocks.translation: This bicycle is lighter than the red one.

spans.value: Ja, men den røde ser mer komfortabel ut.

blocks.translation: Yes, but the red one looks more comfortable.

spans.value: Den korte ruta er brattere. Vi må sykle saktere der.

blocks.translation: The short route is steeper. We must cycle more slowly there.

spans.value: Den lange ruta er mindre bratt, men den er mer komplisert.

blocks.translation: The long route is less steep, but it is more complicated.

spans.value: Du sykler fortere enn meg, så du kan vente hvis det er nødvendig.

blocks.translation: You cycle faster than I do, so you can wait if necessary.

spans.value: Selvfølgelig. Hvilken sykkel er best for deg?

blocks.translation: Of course. Which bicycle is best for you?

spans.value: Den blå er lettest, men den røde har det beste setet.

blocks.translation: The blue one is lightest, but the red one has the best seat.

spans.value: Da tar du den røde. Hvis vi sykler forsiktig, kommer vi trygt fram.

blocks.translation: Then you take the red one. If we cycle carefully, we’ll arrive safely.

Norwegian uses three degrees of comparison:

items.value: ): comparing two people, things, or actions

no.value: Den blå sykkelen er lettere enn den røde.

en.value: The blue bicycle is lighter than the red one.

spans.value: The same three-way distinction applies to adverbs describing actions:

items.value: Use the base form when you are not comparing.
Use the comparative when one side has more or less of a quality than another.
Use the superlative for the highest or lowest degree within a group.

spans.value: An adjective describes a person or thing. An adverb describes how an action happens.
Some Norwegian forms can function in both roles, so meaning and sentence position matter:

no.value: Syklisten kjørte raskere på flat vei.

en.value: The cyclist rode faster on flat ground.

Several frequent words have irregular comparison forms. These must be learned as complete sets.

no.value: Den røde sykkelen er bedre enn den gamle.

en.value: The red bicycle is better than the old one.

no.value: Dette er den beste sykkelen for lange turer.

en.value: This is the best bicycle for long trips.

spans.value: uses the same irregular comparative and superlative:

en.value: She cycles better after the break.

no.value: Av alle i gruppa sykler hun best.

en.value: Of everyone in the group, she cycles best.
The weather is worse in the mountains.

He sees worse in the dark.
The guide has the smallest backpack.

no.value: Den andre ruta er lengre enn denne.

en.value: The other route is longer than this one.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: choosing a journey to work

spans.value: Now change the situation. Erik is choosing between walking, taking the bus, and cycling to work. Walking is cheap but slow. The bus is comfortable but sometimes unreliable. Cycling is fast, and Erik arrives more efficiently when traffic is heavy.

Without returning to the tables, give the comparative and superlative forms needed to say that one route is shorter, one seat is more comfortable, one cyclist rides better, and one journey is the most efficient.

prompt.value: Mina and Jonas are evaluating bicycles, routes, and cycling styles. Classify each Norwegian statement as a base description with no comparison, a comparison between two alternatives, or the highest or lowest degree in a group. Do not infer the category from a word ending alone.

explanation.value: A base form describes without comparing, a comparative sets two alternatives against each other, and a superlative identifies an extreme within a group.

buckets.label: Highest or lowest degree in a group

items.text: Den blå sykkelen er lettere enn den røde.

prompt.value: The bicycle shop has pairs differing in weight, speed, price, and route length. In order, complete each two-way comparison with the regular -ere form and the connector that introduces the second side. The connector is tested where it is blank.

explanation.value: Use -ere for a regular two-way comparison and introduce the second side with enn.

prompt.value: Mina and Jonas are choosing among several bicycles and routes. In order, complete statements identifying the lightest bicycle, fastest cyclist, cheapest bicycle, and shortest route. Use the short -est form after the verb and the required -e form before a definite noun.

explanation.value: Use the short superlative after er, but add -e before a definite noun: sykkelen er billigst, den billigste sykkelen.

prompt.value: Complete paired statements. Choose the form that belongs in the person or thing frame, or in the action frame. In order, the blanks refer to a faster cyclist, Mina cycling better than before, a more comfortable neuter seat, and sitting more comfortably. The scored decision is adjective versus adverb; comparison degree is supporting context.

explanation.value: Use an adjective for a person or thing and an adverb for how an action happens; neuter adjective and regular adverb forms often end in -t.

prompt.value: The rental shop describes several bicycles and plans. Complete the five Norwegian sentences. In order, the intended meanings are lighter, cheapest, more comfortable, most modern, and more efficient. Choose between regular suffix comparison and mer/mest according to the meaning and sentence frame.

explanation.value: Use -ere or -est with common short adjectives; longer adjectives commonly use mer for two-way comparison and mest for a group extreme.

prompt.value: Mina, Jonas, and a guide perform actions in different ways. Complete each action-focused sentence. In order, the meanings are more precisely, most precisely, more efficiently, and more comfortably. Every blank must describe how an action happens, not an object.
Complete each sentence. The base form appears in parentheses. Select the taught irregular comparative or superlative that fits the sentence.

explanation.value: Learn these sets as families: god–bedre–best, dårlig–verre–verst, stor–større–størst, liten–mindre–minst, lang–lengre–lengst, mye–mer–mest.

spans.value: Av de tre syklene er den grønne den (god)
Av alle dagene blir været på søndag (dårlig)
Av alle i laget trener guiden (mye)

prompt.value: Erik is choosing between walking, taking the bus, and cycling to work. Write a short Norwegian comparison in this new commuting situation. Compare price, speed, comfort, reliability, distance, and how efficiently Erik travels. Include at least one comparison between two alternatives and at least one highest- or lowest-degree statement across all three alternatives. Use regular, long, and irregular adjective and adverb comparison patterns. For reliability, you may express the comparison through how well an option functions. Use natural Bokmål and do not copy a complete sentence from the bicycle-trip dialogue.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian response against the commuting task and report evidence for every criterion. Accept natural Bokmål wording when it preserves the requested comparison meaning and target pattern.

criteria.instruction: Addresses price, speed, comfort, reliability, distance, and travel efficiency across the three commuting options.
Includes at least one comparison between two alternatives and at least one highest- or lowest-degree statement across all three alternatives.
Uses at least one accurate regular -ere or -est form, one mer or mest form, and one taught irregular comparison form.
Uses an adjective to compare a travel option and an adverb to compare how Erik travels.
Keeps the comparisons in Erik's commuting situation rather than copying the lesson's bicycle-trip sentences.
